derivations.method: Report is printed as '20:20/00:20Z' at JFK with no day marker. Converted local 2026-09-16T20:20 at JFK via to_utc, giving 2026-09-17T00:20Z — the printed Zulu time of day is correct but falls on the following calendar day.
Report is printed as '00:25/23:25Z' at LHR. Converted local 2026-09-27T00:25 (BST) via to_utc, giving 2026-09-26T23:25Z — the Zulu date is the PREVIOUS day.
Off duty printed '19:05/00:05Z' at ORD with no '+1'. Converted local 2026-09-04T19:05 via to_utc, giving 2026-09-05T00:05Z.
Off duty printed '00:27/23:27Z+1'. The '+1' belongs to the local reading; to_utc on 2026-09-08T00:27 at LHR returns 2026-09-07T23:27Z, so the UTC date is unchanged.
STA/off duty printed '06:35/22:35Z+1' and '07:05/23:05Z+1' at SIN. to_utc on 2026-09-19T06:35 and 07:05 Singapore returns 2026-09-18T22:35Z and 2026-09-18T23:05Z — same UTC day despite the '+1'.
STA '00:50/23:50Z+1' converts to 2026-09-20T23:50Z (same UTC day) while off duty '01:20/00:20Z+1' converts to 2026-09-21T00:20Z (next UTC day) — the two '+1' markers resolve to different Zulu dates.
Off duty '09:30/08:30Z+1' at LHR after an overnight ORD-LHR sector; to_utc on 2026-09-06T09:30 gives 2026-09-06T08:30Z.
SIM training: report taken as the printed window start 08:00/07:00Z with NO reporting offset applied, since the crew member is due at the simulator venue rather than reporting for a flight.
